title: MLC retirement income product reaches $1.2bn FUM
full_text:
Helping clients turn superannuation savings into retirement income has emerged as a focus for advisers using MLC Expand, with its Retirement Boost product reaching $1.2 billion in funds under management a year after launch.
MLC director of retirement innovation Ashton Jones said the growth reflected a shift in retirement planning, as attention moved from building balances towards understanding how much income those savings could deliver.
“For a long time, retirement has been framed around accumulation. The next challenge is helping Australians understand what they can receive in retirement, so they can live life with more confidence rather than hold back because they are worried about running out,” Jones said.
The product, developed with TAL and Challenger, allows clients to move between a superannuation savings phase and a pension phase designed to provide income for life. Its pension component can operate independently or alongside an account-based pension.
MLC Expand said Retirement Boost had become the fastest growing innovative retirement income stream (IRIS) product on a wrap platform, with chief executive Liz McCarthy pointing to demand for options that advisers could incorporate into their existing client relationships.
“Retirement is one of the biggest financial challenges facing Australians, and advisers are looking for practical ways to help clients feel more confident about the income they can receive in retirement,” McCarthy said.
“What has been pleasing is that advisers are not just seeing MLC Retirement Boost as another product. They are seeing it as a practical way to have a different conversation with clients about confidence, certainty and how they can make more of their super in retirement.”
Alongside lifetime income, the product’s design potentially enables clients to access Age Pension means test concessions during its superannuation phase, which otherwise operates like a standard super account.
According to MLC Expand, combining Retirement Boost with traditional retirement products such as an account-based pension can provide up to 60 per cent more income in retirement.
The release cited Chant West research finding that strategies incorporating the product could deliver higher annual income through a combination of payments continuing for life and higher Age Pension payments.
Jones said advisers’ ability to explain and implement retirement income strategies depended on the support available alongside the product.
“That is why it’s not just the product, but the service model that matters. Advisers need more than a strong product. They need education, tools, technical support and a platform experience that makes it easier to bring these conversations to life with clients.”
That support includes MLC Expand’s Centre of Excellence, established through the partnership with TAL and Challenger, which provides technical insights, case studies, calculators, client support tools and dedicated assistance.
MLC Expand has continued to develop the service and recently introduced an Income Deferral feature, with further product changes planned over the next 12 months.
